key_insight: By replacing the traditional isotropic stress assumption with a shearing-only constitutive relation, the corrected Navier-Stokes model changes near-wall turbulence dynamics and removes the mean-velocity overshoot seen in standard DNS.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a more physically faithful framework for predicting wall-bounded turbulence, with potential impact on CFD models for channels, pipes, and other shear-dominated flows.
method: DNS of fully developed turbulent channel flow at Re_tau = 550
Compare corrected Navier-Stokes (CNS) against traditional Navier-Stokes (TNS) results
Analyze mean flow, turbulence statistics, instantaneous coherent structures, and SPOD spectra
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that CNS-DNS matches the turbulent channel flow data better near the wall, shifts inner/buffer-layer boundaries toward the wall, suppresses the TNS velocity overshoot, and reveals coherent-structure changes through VGT and SPOD analysis.
watch_item: The corrected constitutive assumption is still specialized and validated here only for a single channel-flow Reynolds number, so broader applicability and numerical robustness need further testing.
paper_title: Direct Numerical Simulation of Fully Developed Turbulent Channel Flow Based on the Corrected Navier-Stokes Equations
